chunks: They ask you, 'What is lawful for them?' Say, 'Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the hunting beasts, training them as Allah has taught you; so eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for eating meat from trained hunting animals in Islam?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in the context of the Meccan or Medinan period, establishes the permissibility of hunting with trained beasts of prey, provided the owner recites Allah's name at the release. Shia scholars emphasize the condition of 'Tasmiyah' (mentioning Allah's name) as a spiritual safeguard against consuming what was not slaughtered in His name, linking physical sustenance to divine consciousness (Taqwa).
